Subject: Onboarding paperwork — PO requirement during pilot?

Hi Priya,

Quick question as we're kicking off the PilotWorks <> Redwood pilot next week: do we need to issue a purchase order (PO) to cover the pilot period or is there an invoice-only path for short pilots? Our procurement team typically insists on a PO for any vendor engagement but this is a proof-of-concept with no committed spend yet.

We attached our vendor intake form. Also, we can share SOC 2 / IP assurances if needed. If a PO is required, what fields/values does Redwood need on it (billing address, legal name, tax ID)? If an exception is possible, what's the approval cadence?

Thanks — want to avoid any last-minute billing holds.

Regards,
Maya Rao
Procurement Lead, PilotWorks
procure@pilotworks.com

From: Priya Natarajan <priya@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Onboarding paperwork — PO requirement during pilot?

Hi Maya — thanks for the note and for sending the intake. Copying Finance and Procurement Ops to keep this moving.

Short answer: we prefer a PO for paid engagements, but we do offer an "invoice-only" onboarding path for short pilots provided certain conditions are met and Procurement approves a temporary PO-exception. Typical conditions we require for an invoice-only pilot:
- Spend cap for the pilot period (suggest $5k unless you propose otherwise)
- Signed vendor intake and proof of tax ID / legal entity (we need the W-9 or equivalent)
- Acceptance of our standard pilot terms (we can accept via email acknowledgement if you cannot sign the full MSA yet)
- A procurement owner at PilotWorks who will generate a PO later if you convert to paid committed usage

Next steps from our side:
1) Please return the completed intake AND attach your company tax ID/W-9.
2) Confirm requested pilot spend cap and point of contact for billing.
3) We'll route a PO-exception request through procurement ops. Diego, Marissa — can you weigh in on risk/threshold here? I attached our pilot evidence checklist to speed review.

If PilotWorks insists on a PO upfront, include the legal name (PilotWorks, Inc.), tax ID, billing address, and a reference field "PW-2027-PILOT-42".

Happy to chat on a quick call if helpful.

Best,
Priya Natarajan
Senior Procurement Manager
Redwood Inference
priya@redwood.com

Priya, Diego — reviewing PilotWorks' intake and W-9. They look like typical small-pilot profile. Some quick notes from Finance:
- Risk appetite for invoice-only pilots remains low for new vendors unless preapproved by Procurement Ops.
- Proposed controls we recommend: capped net 30 invoice for pilot phase, no auto-renew into paid, finance triggers a PO request if usage exceeds the cap.

I've sketched an "exception matrix" that maps vendor maturity and pilot risk to approval authority (Procurement Ops vs Head of Finance). For this case, PilotWorks falls into the "low-risk, new vendor" cell and would require Diego's signoff for an exception up to $10k.

I've attached the draft matrix and highlighted the proposed conditions:
1) $5k pilot cap; 2) PO must be opened within 10 business days if the pilot converts; 3) a billing point-of-contact and statement of work (SOW) for any paid work.

Diego — can you approve the exception with those conditions or propose edits? If you approve, Procurement Ops will issue an official PO-exception PDF for PilotWorks to countersign.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Finance Operations Manager
marissa@redwood.com

Thanks — reviewed. Approving a PO-exception for PilotWorks under the following conditions:
- Pilot spend cap: $5,000 total across the pilot window.
- Payment terms: Net 30 for pilot invoices; single invoice allowed covering pilot usage.
- PO issuance: PilotWorks must generate a PO within 10 business days if they convert to paid; Redwood Finance will not process additional invoices beyond the cap without a PO.
- SOW: Any paid integration work requires an SOW signed by both parties before additional spend.
- Retain intake + W-9 in vendor file; require SOC 2 link or equivalent before converting.

Priya / Marissa — I'll generate the official PO-exception approval PDF and route it to PilotWorks for countersignature. HubSpot note: https://hubspot.company/deal/PW-2027-PILOT-42. DocuSign request queued: https://app.docusign.com/ABC123456789
